consumer: The engine's detection/targeting eligibility logic (monster-AI / target-selection / can-attack gate) asking the yes/no 'can the avatar see THIS creature right now?' as computed by Creature::sees().
scope: A single ordered creature pair: avatar -> this specific nearby monster, at the avatar's current position and turn; not a region scan, not on-person inventory.
decisive_source: src/creature.cpp::Creature::sees(const Creature&) — its body computes a single boolean visibility verdict from range (rl_dist), light, line of sight (here.sees), hallucination/dimension, and concealment/crouch/hide checks; the engine-returned bool IS the authority.
divergence: A monster that is inside the export window and at full hp (so Excerpt 3 includes it and Excerpt 1 writes positive hp) but stands behind an opaque wall or is hidden by darkness/concealment so Creature::sees() returns false: an answer derived from in-window presence or raw position rather than the sees() verdict would falsely report 'visible'.
